panels.description: Click to move the origin. Press play on the bar below: the clock is the time of day of the journey, and 07:00 is departure. Pause, and the four numbers underneath move to that moment.

targets.rawSql:
-- Cobertura por bandas de 5 min, sin filtrar por el reloj: la sombra.
SELECT minutos, ST_AsHEXWKB(geom) AS geom
FROM ST_Read('http://iso-cuenca:8099/iso.geojson?' || 'lat=' || $lat || '&lon=' || $lng || '&date=' || $fecha ||
         '&calle=' || $calle || '&transit=${publico:csv}' ||
         '&walk=' || $apie || '&rides=' || $trasbordos || '&step=5&max=' || $cutoff);

-- Una fila por celda alcanzable, con el minuto en que se alcanza
-- convertido a hora de reloj desde la salida (07:00).
SELECT minutos, geom,
       (($fecha || ' 07:00:00')::TIMESTAMP
        + INTERVAL (minutos) MINUTE) AS t
FROM read_json_auto('http://iso-cuenca:8099/cells.json?' || 'lat=' || $lat || '&lon=' || $lng || '&date=' || $fecha ||
         '&calle=' || $calle || '&transit=${publico:csv}' ||
         '&walk=' || $apie || '&rides=' || $trasbordos || '&max=' || $cutoff);

panels.title: Accessibility from wherever you click — the query's window, animated

panels.description: R5's own measure, not a count of ours: opportunities from the population grid within the threshold. It follows the map's clock: pause the animation wherever you like and the number moves to that moment. Before the first play it shows the cutoff.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT personas FROM read_json_auto('http://iso-cuenca:8099/accessibility.json?' || 'lat=' || $lat || '&lon=' || $lng || '&date=' || $fecha ||
         '&calle=' || $calle || '&transit=${publico:csv}' ||
         '&walk=' || $apie || '&rides=' || $trasbordos) WHERE minutos = least(coalesce(date_diff('minute', ($fecha || ' 07:00:00')::TIMESTAMP,
                 try_cast(try_cast($t_fin AS TIMESTAMPTZ) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS TIMESTAMP)),
               try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER)),
      try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER));

panels.title: Population

panels.description: Stops from the GTFS feeds whose cell is reached within the threshold. It follows the map's clock: pause the animation wherever you like and the number moves to that moment. Before the first play it shows the cutoff.

targets.rawSql:
WITH alcance AS (
  SELECT min(c.minutos) AS m
  FROM (SELECT unnest(stops) AS s FROM read_json_auto('http://r5-gateway/api/gtfs/6a976415196cd834c785ad5d/stops')) p
  JOIN (SELECT minutos, ST_GeomFromHEXWKB(geom) AS g
        FROM read_json_auto('http://iso-cuenca:8099/cells.json?' || 'lat=' || $lat || '&lon=' || $lng || '&date=' || $fecha ||
         '&calle=' || $calle || '&transit=${publico:csv}' ||
         '&walk=' || $apie || '&rides=' || $trasbordos || '&max=' || $cutoff)) c
    ON ST_Within(ST_Point(p.s.lon, p.s.lat), c.g)
  GROUP BY p.s._id
)
SELECT count(*) AS paradas FROM alcance WHERE m <= least(coalesce(date_diff('minute', ($fecha || ' 07:00:00')::TIMESTAMP,
                 try_cast(try_cast($t_fin AS TIMESTAMPTZ) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS TIMESTAMP)),
               try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER)),
      try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER));

panels.title: Transit stops

panels.description: Parks with at least one entrance within the threshold, out of 381. The park is counted, not the gate. It follows the map's clock: pause the animation wherever you like and the number moves to that moment. Before the first play it shows the cutoff.

targets.rawSql:
WITH parques AS (
  SELECT p.park_id, min(c.minutos) AS m
  FROM ST_Read('https://appsllactalab.ucuenca.edu.ec/geoserver/geonode/puntos_acceso_parques/ows?service=WFS&version=2.0.0&request=GetFeature&typeNames=geonode:puntos_acceso_parques&outputFormat=application/json&srsName=EPSG:4326') p
  JOIN (SELECT minutos, ST_GeomFromHEXWKB(geom) AS g
        FROM read_json_auto('http://iso-cuenca:8099/cells.json?' || 'lat=' || $lat || '&lon=' || $lng || '&date=' || $fecha ||
         '&calle=' || $calle || '&transit=${publico:csv}' ||
         '&walk=' || $apie || '&rides=' || $trasbordos || '&max=' || $cutoff)) c
    ON ST_Within(p.geom, c.g)
  WHERE p.situacion IS DISTINCT FROM 'RESERVA'
  GROUP BY p.park_id
)
SELECT count(*) AS parques FROM parques WHERE m <= least(coalesce(date_diff('minute', ($fecha || ' 07:00:00')::TIMESTAMP,
                 try_cast(try_cast($t_fin AS TIMESTAMPTZ) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS TIMESTAMP)),
               try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER)),
      try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER));

panels.title: Parks

panels.description: The true area of the reached cells, summed. It follows the map's clock: pause the animation wherever you like and the number moves to that moment. Before the first play it shows the cutoff.

targets.rawSql:
WITH celdas AS (
  SELECT minutos,
         ST_Area(ST_Transform(ST_GeomFromHEXWKB(geom), 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:3857',
                              always_xy := true))
           / 1e6 * pow(cos(radians(try_cast($lat AS DOUBLE))), 2) AS km2
  FROM read_json_auto('http://iso-cuenca:8099/cells.json?' || 'lat=' || $lat || '&lon=' || $lng || '&date=' || $fecha ||
         '&calle=' || $calle || '&transit=${publico:csv}' ||
         '&walk=' || $apie || '&rides=' || $trasbordos || '&max=' || $cutoff)
)
SELECT round(sum(km2), 1) AS km2 FROM celdas WHERE minutos <= least(coalesce(date_diff('minute', ($fecha || ' 07:00:00')::TIMESTAMP,
                 try_cast(try_cast($t_fin AS TIMESTAMPTZ) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS TIMESTAMP)),
               try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER)),
      try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER));

panels.title: Area

panels.description: Cumulative, in five-minute steps up to the cutoff. The red dot is where the map's clock currently is.

targets.rawSql:
WITH marcas AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT m FROM (
    SELECT unnest(generate_series(0, try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER), 5)) AS m
    UNION ALL SELECT least(coalesce(date_diff('minute', ($fecha || ' 07:00:00')::TIMESTAMP,
                 try_cast(try_cast($t_fin AS TIMESTAMPTZ) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS TIMESTAMP)),
               try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER)),
      try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER))
  ) WHERE m BETWEEN 0 AND try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER)
)
SELECT marcas.m AS minutos, a.personas,
       CASE WHEN marcas.m = least(coalesce(date_diff('minute', ($fecha || ' 07:00:00')::TIMESTAMP,
                 try_cast(try_cast($t_fin AS TIMESTAMPTZ) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS TIMESTAMP)),
               try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER)),
      try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER)) THEN a.personas END AS "at the playhead"
FROM marcas JOIN read_json_auto('http://iso-cuenca:8099/accessibility.json?' || 'lat=' || $lat || '&lon=' || $lng || '&date=' || $fecha ||
         '&calle=' || $calle || '&transit=${publico:csv}' ||
         '&walk=' || $apie || '&rides=' || $trasbordos) a ON a.minutos = marcas.m
ORDER BY marcas.m;

WITH alcance AS (
  SELECT min(c.minutos) AS m
  FROM (SELECT unnest(stops) AS s FROM read_json_auto('http://r5-gateway/api/gtfs/6a976415196cd834c785ad5d/stops')) p
  JOIN (SELECT minutos, ST_GeomFromHEXWKB(geom) AS g
        FROM read_json_auto('http://iso-cuenca:8099/cells.json?' || 'lat=' || $lat || '&lon=' || $lng || '&date=' || $fecha ||
         '&calle=' || $calle || '&transit=${publico:csv}' ||
         '&walk=' || $apie || '&rides=' || $trasbordos || '&max=' || $cutoff)) c
    ON ST_Within(ST_Point(p.s.lon, p.s.lat), c.g)
  GROUP BY p.s._id
),
marcas AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT m FROM (
    SELECT unnest(generate_series(0, try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER), 5)) AS m
    UNION ALL SELECT least(coalesce(date_diff('minute', ($fecha || ' 07:00:00')::TIMESTAMP,
                 try_cast(try_cast($t_fin AS TIMESTAMPTZ) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS TIMESTAMP)),
               try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER)),
      try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER))
  ) WHERE m BETWEEN 0 AND try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER)
)
SELECT marcas.m AS minutos,
       count(alcance.m) AS paradas,
       CASE WHEN marcas.m = least(coalesce(date_diff('minute', ($fecha || ' 07:00:00')::TIMESTAMP,
                 try_cast(try_cast($t_fin AS TIMESTAMPTZ) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS TIMESTAMP)),
               try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER)),
      try_cast($cutoff AS INTEGER)) THEN count(alcance.m) END AS "at the playhead"
FROM marcas LEFT JOIN alcance ON alcance.m <= marcas.m
GROUP BY marcas.m ORDER BY marcas.m;

panels.title: Area reachable

options.content:
## What this dashboard does

Click anywhere on the map and it answers one question for that spot: **where can you get to by
public transport, and how much is within reach?** The isochrone is drawn for the date, modes and
limits set at the top, and the timeline animates the journey minute by minute from a 07:00
departure — the four figures below the map move with the playhead, and the four charts beside them
accumulate in five-minute steps.

## How it is built

Nothing is precomputed and there is no ETL. Each panel is a DuckDB query issued straight against
three HTTP services:

1. **R5** (Conveyal), behind `r5-gateway`, computes the travel-time surface from the origin for the
   selected date, modes, walk/bike limit and number of rides.
2. **iso-cuenca** turns that surface into two things a query can read: `iso.geojson`, the isochrone
   polygons the map draws, and `cells.json`, every reached cell with the minute it is reached.
   `accessibility.json` returns R5's own opportunity counts.
3. **DuckDB** reads those endpoints in place with `read_json_auto` and `ST_Read`, and joins them
   against the GTFS stops served by R5's own API and the park entrances published as WFS by
   Llactalab (Universidad de Cuenca).

The map is the **Kepler Geospatial Maps** panel, and two of its cross-filtering channels are what
make the dashboard interactive:

- **Clicking publishes a coordinate.** The click is written into `$​lat` and `$​lng`, which every
  query reads — so one click re-answers the whole dashboard for a new origin.
- **The time slider publishes a window.** Instead of moving the dashboard's time range, the map
  writes its playhead into `$​t_ini` and `$​t_fin`, which is how the figures track the animation
  without re-running anything else.

## Reading the numbers

**Population** is R5's own accessibility measure over its population grid, not a count of ours.
**Parks** counts the park once, however many of its entrances fall inside the isochrone, out of 381.
**Area** sums the true surface of the reached cells. Before the first play, all four show the value
at the cutoff.

title: Transit accessibility by isochrone (R5 + DuckDB)
description: Public-transport accessibility from wherever you click. R5 (r5-gateway) computes the travel-time surface, the iso-cuenca service turns it into cells and polygons, and DuckDB does the rest. The map's clock walks the minutes of the journey.
